## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The ASCII-only character class in `slugify` drops accented letters and turns all-non-Latin titles into an empty slug, which contradicts the pull-request description. The description also lacks the `## Testing` section that AGENTS.md requires.

## Changes
The pull request adds `app/slug.py`, which has a `slugify` function that lowercases a title, collapses runs of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` into one hyphen, and trims hyphens from both ends. It also adds parametrized tests in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters and digits in slugs — `slugify("Café Menu")` returns `"caf-menu"`, and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. The description says only "non-alphanumeric characters" are replaced, but `"é".isalnum()` is `True`. — Titles in non-English languages get broken slugs, and all non-Latin titles share the empty slug, so their page URLs collide. — Fix: Either match Unicode word characters, for example with `re.sub(r"[\W_]+", "-", title.lower())`, or transliterate first with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)`; add a non-ASCII case to `test_slugify` either way.
- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the description — The description does not have the section that AGENTS.md:4 requires: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Maintainers can't tell from the description whether or how the change was verified.
